explanation_en: An extremely common idiomatic expression meaning to make a decisive move, take a major step forward, or make a difficult decision after hesitation. It is often used in personal, professional, or social contexts when someone finally overcomes fear or doubt to act.

examples.en_text: After thinking about it a lot, I finally took the plunge and quit my job to open my own shop.
examples.target_text: Después de pensarlo mucho, finalmente di el paso y renuncié a mi trabajo para abrir mi propia tienda.

examples.en_text: They have been dating for five years, but they still don't dare to take the plunge and live together.
examples.target_text: Llevan cinco años de novios, pero todavía no se animan a dar el paso de vivir juntos.

examples.en_text: If you really want to learn English, you have to take the plunge and go live abroad.
examples.target_text: Si quieres aprender inglés de verdad, tienes que dar el paso e irte a vivir al extranjero.

examples.en_text: I would like to buy an apartment, but I'm afraid to take the plunge with the current economic situation.
examples.target_text: Me gustaría comprar un apartamento, pero me da miedo dar el paso con la situación económica actual.

examples.en_text: My parents always wanted to learn to dance salsa, and last week they finally took the plunge.
examples.target_text: Mis padres siempre quisieron aprender a bailar salsa, y la semana pasada por fin dieron el paso.

examples.en_text: It is important for small businesses to take the plunge towards digitalization so they don't get left behind.
examples.target_text: Es importante que las pequeñas empresas den el paso hacia la digitalización para no quedarse atrás.

explanation_en: While 'protagonista' literally means 'protagonist' or 'main character' in a play or movie, in everyday Spanish and journalism, it is widely used to describe the central element, cause, or key player of an event or crisis. It is a natural way to avoid more repetitive words like 'centro' or 'causa.' It is always followed by the preposition 'de.'

examples.en_text: The young forward was the main player in the team's great victory.
examples.target_text: El joven delantero fue el protagonista de la gran victoria del equipo.

examples.en_text: She didn't want to be at the center of the argument, so she preferred to stay quiet.
examples.target_text: Ella no quería ser la protagonista de la discusión, así que prefirió quedarse callada.

examples.en_text: The neighborhood residents were the main players in the reconstruction of the park.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos del barrio fueron los protagonistas de la reconstrucción del parque.

examples.en_text: This new product will be at the center of our next marketing campaign.
examples.target_text: Este nuevo producto será el protagonista de nuestra próxima campaña de marketing.

examples.en_text: The women of the community were the main players in the educational reform.
examples.target_text: Las mujeres de la comunidad fueron las protagonistas de la reforma educativa.

examples.en_text: The strong wind was the main feature of the day, causing several problems.
examples.target_text: El fuerte viento fue el gran protagonista de la jornada, causando varios problemas.

explanation_en: This idiom comes from the 'mira' (sight) of a gun, meaning to be targeted or in the crosshairs. However, in media and general usage, it often carries the broader meaning of being under close scrutiny, in the spotlight, or the focus of attention. It is typically paired with verbs like 'poner' (to put) or 'estar' (to be).

examples.en_text: The team's coach is in the spotlight after losing three games in a row.
examples.target_text: El entrenador del equipo está en el punto de mira tras perder tres partidos seguidos.

examples.en_text: The new education law is under scrutiny by all the teachers.
examples.target_text: La nueva ley de educación está en el punto de mira de todos los profesores.

examples.en_text: Since he announced his resignation, the president has been in the media spotlight.
examples.target_text: Desde que anunció su dimisión, el presidente ha estado en el punto de mira de los medios.

examples.en_text: If you don't submit the report on time, you will be in the director's crosshairs.
examples.target_text: Si no entregas el informe a tiempo, estarás en el punto de mira de la directora.

examples.en_text: Social networks are in the spotlight for how they handle user data.
examples.target_text: Las redes sociales están en el punto de mira por cómo manejan los datos de los usuarios.

examples.en_text: The tourism sector is under scrutiny due to the rise in prices this summer.
examples.target_text: El sector turístico está en el punto de mira debido al aumento de los precios este verano.

explanation_en: This expression means to obtain a benefit, profit, or competitive edge from a situation. Unlike 'aprovecharse de' (which can sometimes carry a negative, exploitative nuance), 'sacar ventaja' is often used in strategic, political, or sports contexts to denote leveraging a position of strength. Avoid using 'tomar ventaja,' which is a literal translation from English and considered an anglicism in many regions.

examples.en_text: Our company managed to take advantage of the situation and launch the product before the competition.
examples.target_text: Nuestra empresa logró sacar ventaja de la situación y lanzar el producto antes que la competencia.

examples.en_text: He is very fast and always gains an advantage in the first meters of the race.
examples.target_text: Él es muy rápido y siempre saca ventaja en los primeros metros de la carrera.

examples.en_text: Don't let them take advantage of your lack of experience in this business.
examples.target_text: No dejes que saquen ventaja de tu falta de experiencia en este negocio.

examples.en_text: Studying during the holidays helped me get ahead of my classmates.
examples.target_text: Estudiar durante las vacaciones me sirvió para sacar ventaja a mis compañeros de clase.

examples.en_text: She always tries to take advantage of any mistake we make.
examples.target_text: Ella siempre intenta sacar ventaja de cualquier error que cometamos.

examples.en_text: If you learn to use this software, you are going to gain an advantage in the job market.
examples.target_text: Si aprendes a usar este programa, vas a sacar ventaja en el mercado laboral.

explanation_en: This is a very common idiomatic collocation used to describe a situation that suddenly triggers widespread concern, anxiety, or warning signs among a group or the public. It is frequently used in journalism, economics, and politics. A common alternative with a similar meaning is 'disparar las alarmas.'

examples.en_text: The sudden increase in flu cases raised alarm bells in the region's hospitals.
examples.target_text: El aumento repentino de casos de gripe encendió las alarmas en los hospitales de la región.

examples.en_text: The drop in sales during the last month set off alarms in the board of directors.
examples.target_text: La caída de las ventas durante el último mes encendió las alarmas en la junta directiva.

examples.en_text: His sudden change of attitude raised alarm bells for his family and friends.
examples.target_text: Su cambio de actitud tan repentino encendió las alarmas de su familia y amigos.

examples.en_text: The strange email I received this morning set off all my alarms.
examples.target_text: El extraño correo electrónico que recibí esta mañana encendió todas mis alarmas.

examples.en_text: The lack of rain during the winter has raised alarm bells in the agricultural sector.
examples.target_text: La falta de lluvias durante el invierno ha encendido las alarmas en el sector agrícola.

examples.en_text: The star player's injury just days before the final set off alarms in the team.
examples.target_text: La lesión del jugador estrella a pocos días de la final encendió las alarmas en el equipo.

explanation_en: This highly common phrasal verb ('echarse atrás') means to retract a promise, decision, or statement, or to retreat from an action due to fear, pressure, or a change of mind. It is widely used in both informal speech and formal news reporting. It is important to conjugate the reflexive pronoun 'se' to match the subject (e.g., 'me eché atrás', 'se echaron atrás').

examples.en_text: We had planned to travel this weekend, but when he saw the price of the flights, he quickly backed out.
examples.target_text: Habíamos planeado viajar este fin de semana, pero cuando vio el precio de los vuelos, se echó rápidamente atrás.

examples.en_text: I was going to sign the rental contract, but when I read the clauses, I quickly backed out.
examples.target_text: Iba a firmar el contrato de alquiler, pero cuando leí las cláusulas, me eché rápidamente atrás.

examples.en_text: The investors promised to support our project, but at the last minute they quickly backed down.
examples.target_text: Los inversores prometieron apoyar nuestro proyecto, pero a última hora se echaron rápidamente atrás.

examples.en_text: You said you would help me with the move, but when you saw how many boxes there were, you quickly backed out.
examples.target_text: Dijiste que me ayudarías con la mudanza, pero cuando viste cuántas cajas había, te echaste rápidamente atrás.

examples.en_text: We wanted to protest the schedule change, but seeing the boss's reaction, we quickly backed down.
examples.target_text: Queríamos protestar por el cambio de horario, pero al ver la reacción del jefe, nos echamos rápidamente atrás.

examples.en_text: She was going to tell her boyfriend the truth, but when she saw him so happy, she quickly backed down.
examples.target_text: Iba a decirle la verdad a su novio, pero cuando lo vio tan feliz, se echó rápidamente atrás.

explanation_en: This formal collocation refers to something that discourages or prevents an action through fear of the consequences (a deterrent). It is derived from the verb 'disuadir' (to dissuade). It is a staple of political, legal, and security-related discourse in Spanish.

examples.en_text: Installing an alarm at home is an excellent deterrent against thieves.
examples.target_text: Instalar una alarma en casa es un excelente elemento disuasorio contra los ladrones.

examples.en_text: High traffic fines are effective deterrents to prevent speeding.
examples.target_text: Las multas de tráfico elevadas son elementos disuasorios eficaces para evitar el exceso de velocidad.

examples.en_text: The presence of security cameras in the store is the best deterrent to prevent theft.
examples.target_text: La presencia de cámaras de seguridad en la tienda es el mejor elemento disuasorio para evitar los robos.

examples.en_text: Punishment shouldn't just be a deterrent, but also an opportunity to learn.
examples.target_text: El castigo no debe ser solo un elemento disuasorio, sino también una oportunidad para aprender.

examples.en_text: Many countries maintain a strong army as a deterrent against potential threats.
examples.target_text: Muchos países mantienen un ejército fuerte como un elemento disuasorio frente a posibles amenazas.

examples.en_text: A good password system is an effective deterrent against hackers.
examples.target_text: Un buen sistema de contraseñas es un elemento disuasorio eficaz contra los piratas informáticos.

explanation_en: This elegant idiomatic expression means to emphasize, highlight, or bring something to the forefront of attention. It is highly common in written journalism, academic writing, and formal speech. It functions similarly to 'destacar' or 'poner de manifiesto,' and is a great way to elevate your vocabulary register.

examples.en_text: The latest report highlights the need to make changes in the company.
examples.target_text: El último informe pone de relieve la necesidad de hacer cambios en la empresa.

examples.en_text: The health crisis has highlighted the importance of mental health.
examples.target_text: La crisis sanitaria ha puesto de relieve la importancia de la salud mental.

examples.en_text: The teacher wanted to highlight the great effort of his students.
examples.target_text: El profesor quiso poner de relieve el gran esfuerzo de sus estudiantes.

examples.en_text: This situation only highlights that we must work as a team.
examples.target_text: Esta situación solo pone de relieve que debemos trabajar en equipo.

examples.en_text: The documentary highlights the effects of climate change in the region.
examples.target_text: El documental pone de relieve los efectos del cambio climático en la región.

examples.en_text: Your words highlight your lack of interest in the project.
examples.target_text: Tus palabras ponen de relieve tu falta de interés en el proyecto.

explanation_en: The pronominal verb 'volcarse con' means to go out of one's way to help, support, or show affection to someone. It is highly common in everyday Spanish when talking about communities, friends, or family rallying around someone in need. Note that it always uses the preposition 'con' to indicate the recipient of the support.

examples.en_text: The whole neighborhood has rallied around Pedro's family after the fire at their house.
examples.target_text: Todo el barrio se ha volcado con la familia de Pedro tras el incendio de su casa.

examples.en_text: The company has gone all out for the new sustainability project.
examples.target_text: La empresa se ha volcado con el nuevo proyecto de sostenibilidad.

examples.en_text: Since she started painting, her mother has gone all out for her so she can go to a good school.
examples.target_text: Desde que empezó a pintar, su madre se ha volcado con ella para que pueda ir a una buena escuela.

examples.en_text: My friends have rallied around my brother after his car accident.
examples.target_text: Mis amigos se han volcado con mi hermano tras su accidente de coche.

examples.en_text: The entire town has gone all out for the clothing donation campaign.
examples.target_text: El pueblo entero se ha volcado con la campaña de donación de ropa.

examples.en_text: The school has gone all out for the student who had difficulty adapting.
examples.target_text: El colegio se ha volcado con el alumno que tenía dificultades para adaptarse.

explanation_en: While 'de lujo' literally means 'luxurious' or 'deluxe', colloquially it functions as an adverb meaning 'wonderfully', 'excellently', or 'like royalty'. It is widely used in Spain to describe how someone was treated, how an event went, or how someone feels (e.g., 'estar de lujo').

examples.en_text: In that hotel they treated us wonderfully; they gave us free breakfast every day.
examples.target_text: En ese hotel nos trataron de lujo; nos daban desayuno gratis todos los días.

examples.en_text: That blue dress looks great on you, you should buy it for the wedding.
examples.target_text: Ese vestido azul te queda de lujo, deberías comprarlo para la boda.

examples.en_text: It sounds great to me that we are going to the beach this weekend.
examples.target_text: Me parece de lujo que vayamos a la playa este fin de semana.

examples.en_text: We had a wonderful time at yesterday's concert; the band played all of our favorite songs.
examples.target_text: Lo pasamos de lujo en el concierto de ayer, la banda tocó todas nuestras canciones favoritas.

examples.en_text: We went to an Italian restaurant and had a wonderful dinner for very little money.
examples.target_text: Fuimos a un restaurante italiano y cenamos de lujo por muy poco dinero.

examples.en_text: Since the mechanic fixed the car, the engine has been running perfectly.
examples.target_text: Desde que el mecánico arregló el coche, el motor funciona de lujo.

explanation_en: 'Dar una tregua' means to grant a temporary respite, break, or truce. While it originates from military contexts (a truce), it is very commonly used in weather reports, health contexts, or stressful situations to describe a temporary relief from adversity.

examples.en_text: The weather has given us a break this afternoon and we were able to go for a walk.
examples.target_text: El tiempo nos ha dado una tregua esta tarde y hemos podido salir a caminar.

examples.en_text: Work has finally given me a break this week, so I am going to rest.
examples.target_text: El trabajo por fin me ha dado una tregua esta semana, así que voy a descansar.

examples.en_text: The fever has given the child a break and now he is sleeping peacefully.
examples.target_text: La fiebre le ha dado una tregua al niño y ahora está durmiendo tranquilo.

examples.en_text: It seems that inflation has given us a break this month and prices haven't gone up.
examples.target_text: Parece que la inflación nos ha dado una tregua este mes y los precios no han subido.

examples.en_text: The construction noise has given us a break over the weekend.
examples.target_text: El ruido de las obras nos ha dado una tregua durante el fin de semana.

examples.en_text: My headache has given me a break and I was able to finish the report.
examples.target_text: El dolor de cabeza me ha dado una tregua y he podido terminar el informe.

explanation_en: 'Mantener en vilo' means to keep someone in suspense, on tenterhooks, or in a state of anxious waiting. It is a very common idiomatic expression in news, literature, and daily conversations when describing situations where the outcome is highly uncertain.

examples.en_text: This author's latest novel kept me on tenterhooks from the first page.
examples.target_text: La última novela de este autor me mantuvo en vilo desde la primera página.

examples.en_text: The doctors kept us in suspense for hours until they came out of the operating room.
examples.target_text: Los médicos nos mantuvieron en vilo durante horas hasta que salieron del quirófano.

examples.en_text: The football match was so close that it kept all the spectators on tenterhooks.
examples.target_text: El partido de fútbol estuvo tan reñido que mantuvo en vilo a todos los espectadores.

examples.en_text: The government's decision on taxes is keeping small business owners on tenterhooks.
examples.target_text: La decisión del gobierno sobre los impuestos mantiene en vilo a los pequeños empresarios.

examples.en_text: Don't keep me in suspense any longer, tell me now if they gave you the job or not.
examples.target_text: No me mantengas más en vilo, dime ya si te han dado el trabajo o no.

examples.en_text: The rain forecast is keeping us on tenterhooks because we want to have the wedding outdoors.
examples.target_text: El pronóstico de lluvia nos mantiene en vilo porque queremos celebrar la boda al aire libre.
